slides.0.title: North and south: Coquimbo and the Sur zone
slides.0.subtitle: Elqui, Limarí and Choapa, then Itata, Bío-Bío and Malleco
slides.1.title: Elqui: vineyards at the desert's edge
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Location
slides.1.highlights.0.content: In the Coquimbo Region about 400 km north of Santiago at the southern end of the Atacama Desert, with vineyards running from the Pacific coast to the Andes (Wikipedia)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Climate and altitude
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Wikipedia: a sunny, desert-like climate with under 70 mm of rain a year; vineyards rise to about 2,000 m; strong winds from the Pacific and the Andes cool the hills
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Grapes and pisco
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Wikipedia (c. 2013 data): about 286 ha with Syrah first at 87 ha; Syrah does well in this climate; the area is known for table grapes and pisco, and wine growers only moved north in the 1990s
slides.1.content: Elqui is one of Chile's northernmost wine valleys, where a desert climate is managed by irrigation and altitude.
slides.2.title: Limarí and Choapa
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Limarí's fog
slides.2.highlights.0.content: A semi-arid climate moderated by morning fog known locally as Camanchaca (Wine With Seth); Concha y Toro describes a semi-arid coastal climate with steady sea breezes
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Limestone and minerality
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Concha y Toro: several layers of calcium carbonate in the soils are linked to an intense mineral character; Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir stand out
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Distance and Choapa
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Sources differ on Limarí's distance from Santiago (about 300 or about 470 km), so it is not tested; Choapa appears only by name in this lesson's sources, with no figures to cite
slides.2.content: Limarí's fog and limestone soils make whites of intense minerality.
slides.3.title: Itata: old-vine País and Cinsault
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Location and climate
slides.3.highlights.0.content: In the Ñuble Region, between Maule to the north and Bío-Bío to the south; a humid temperate climate with 800–1,200 mm of rain and altitudes of about 100–400 m (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: An old-vine tradition
slides.3.highlights.1.content: País is the dominant red with vines 80 to over 150 years old; Cinsault arrived in the 19th century; the white Moscatel de Alejandría is used for table wine and pisco; the old vines are mostly dry-farmed bush vines (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: The revival
slides.3.highlights.2.content: About 8,000 ha (Wine With Seth); it declined in the 20th century as premium central-Chile wine rose, and revived from the 2010s — De Martino's Marcelo Retamal began sourcing Itata País and Cinsault around 2010–2012
slides.3.content: Itata is where Chile's old-vine, dry-farmed tradition is being revived.
slides.4.title: Bío-Bío and Malleco: the southern frontier
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Bío-Bío
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Wine With Seth says it shares Itata's grapes and soils (granitic and volcanic), with the same dry-farmed old-vine character
slides.4.highlights.1.title: The Sur zone's role
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Wine With Seth calls the south a "fast-growing frontier" for old-vine País, Carignan, Moscatel and cool-climate varieties; rainfall is enough for dry farming
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Data limits
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Malleco appears only in lists in this lesson's sources, with no area or climate figures to cite, so only its place as part of the southern frontier is tested
slides.4.content: The further south, the wetter and cooler it gets, with old vines and cool-climate varieties side by side.
Elqui lies at the southern end of which desert?
Besides wine, which spirit is the Elqui area known for?
The area is known for table grapes and pisco.
What is Limarí's morning fog called locally?
What is Limarí's intense minerality often linked to?
A. Calcium carbonate in the soils
As described by Concha y Toro.
With vines 80 to over 150 years old.
How are Itata and Bío-Bío positioned?
A. Itata is to the north, Bío-Bío to the south
B. Itata is to the south, Bío-Bío to the north
C. Both lie in the Atacama Desert
D. They are the same valley
Itata borders Maule to the north and Bío-Bío to the south.
